findings.claim: Endpoint-coordinate contrasts at the observed selection nodes are dominated by shape (second-moment) descriptors rather than centroid translation: shape_yy shows the strongest integrated high-low contrast with all batches same-sign, and shape_xx is similarly negative, whereas global_centroid_x and global_centroid_z are indistinguishable from zero.

global_centroid_y carries a smaller but multiplicity-surviving negative integrated contrast, so among translation coordinates only the y component shows a signed favorable-versus-comparison separation; this is a selection-enrichment contrast, not an absolute geometric descriptor.

Continuous contrast functions over the complete observed window are non-monotone: landmark local features show multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts, with first-rate and last-rate z of opposite sign, and no polynomial fit is accepted; the observed-node linear method is the only validated representation and extrapolation is disallowed.

The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary with validity and strain secondary under coordinate-only control, so these coordinate contrasts are steering evidence and not themselves affinity outcomes.

hypotheses.falsifier: A constant rule matching the time-conditioned rule's node-wise sign pattern across the observed window.
hypotheses.scope: observed score window [0.0,0.5], predicted endpoint world coordinates
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule (rate-weighted, using observed-node interpolation) would prioritize shape_yy/shape_xx contrasts differently across the window than a constant whole-window rule, because their first and last rates differ in sign and magnitude.

hypotheses.falsifier: Marginal centroid descriptors showing equal or stronger multiplicity-adjusted signed support than joint shape descriptors.
hypotheses.scope: observed selection nodes, predicted endpoint world coordinates
hypotheses.statement: Joint shape (second-moment) coordinate patterns carry more coherent signed evidence than isolated marginal centroid descriptors, so coupling diagnostics should be consulted before treating centroid shifts as independent targets.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or final affinity outcomes were supplied, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit; the immediate-selection versus descendant-credit comparison is unavailable.
No covariance, intact-conformation or mode diagnostics were read, so joint-versus-marginal coupling claims remain hypotheses rather than established findings.
No parent-child increment or turnover-residual evidence was read, so within-path change versus changing cohort composition cannot be distinguished here.
Contrast curves are coordinate rewards, not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies, and no neural-module causation is implied.
